legend: You are given n$$$n$$$ glasses containing solutions of salt. For each solution, the total mass and the mass of the salt contained within it are known. The objective is to determine the number of non-empty subsets of these n$$$n$$$ glasses such that if their contents are combined into an empty glass, the resulting solution will achieve a specified mass fraction of salt.
input: The first line contains three integers n$$$n$$$, a$$$a$$$, and b$$$b$$$ (2≤n≤35$$$2 \leq n \leq 35$$$, 0≤a≤10000$$$0 \leq a \leq 10\,000$$$, max(a,1)≤b≤10000$$$\max(a, 1) \leq b \leq 10\,000$$$, gcd(a,b)=1$$$\text{gcd}(a, b) = 1$$$) — the number of glasses containing solutions, the numerator, and the denominator of the fraction ab$$$\frac{a}{b}$$$ representing the desired mass fraction of salt, respectively.

The following n$$$n$$$ lines each contain two integers mi$$$m_i$$$ and ti$$$t_i$$$ (0≤mi≤10000$$$0 \leq m_i \leq 10\,000$$$, max(mi,1)≤ti≤10000$$$\max(m_i, 1) \leq t_i \leq 10\,000$$$) — the mass of salt and the total mass of the i$$$i$$$-th solution (i=1,2,…,n$$$i = 1, 2, \ldots, n$$$).
output: Output a single integer – the number of ways to achieve a solution with a mass fraction of salt ab$$$\frac{a}{b}$$$.
